claim: Out-of-scope change creates a security hole. `MessagePackSecurity.GetEqualityComparer<T>` used to throw `TypeAccessException` for types that have no hash-collision-resistant comparer. It now silently returns `EqualityComparer<T>.Default`. Under `MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData`, deserializing a dictionary or hash set keyed by an arbitrary type therefore uses a non-resistant comparer, which re-opens the hash-flooding DoS that this guard closed. REQ-2129 asks for nothing in this area, and the change contradicts the secure-by-default history recorded in L12.

It passes on base and fails on head because no exception is thrown.

claim: The acceptance criterion 'If T does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured' is not met. `Collect` never looks at attributes on T. Without a surrogate it always calls `CreateContractlessMembers`, which takes every public read-write member, uses its name as a string key, and sorts ordinally. As a result, `[MessagePackObject]` with `[Key(int)]` keys is ignored and the wire format changes from an array to a map. `[IgnoreMember]` members are serialized. `[DataContract]`/`[DataMember]` membership and names are ignored, so non-`[DataMember]` public members are serialized. The maintainer note only allows contractless mode when T has no `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]`.

claim: GetEqualityComparer's fallback for unknown types now returns EqualityComparer<T>.Default instead of throwing TypeAccessException. It is also a behavioral change for existing users, and the requirement does not ask for it.

claim: The contractless mode orders members by ordinal name and assigns int keys 0..n-1. Members are only public read-write ones, so read-only properties and fields are dropped. The wire format for contractless types is therefore not the same as the dynamic contractless resolver. Pre-existing hand-written or reflection formatters for the same type will produce different bytes (string-key maps compared with the dynamic resolver's ordering and read-only handling).

claim: The requirement says contractless behaviour over public members, but the generated formatter covers less than MessagePack's existing contractless mode. `IsPublicReadWrite` drops every get-only or init-less public property, so these members are silently not serialized at all, even on the serialize side. In addition, a class whose only constructor takes parameters (for example a positional record, common in dependency-free libraries) is rejected with MsgPack007 instead of matching constructor parameters by name as `ContractlessStandardResolver` does. Immutable public types from Project A therefore lose data or get no formatter.
